name: Delaware Water Gap Toll Bridge
connectingPointsDisplay: Hardwick Township, NJ — Delaware Water Gap, PA
facts: The Delaware Water Gap Toll Bridge, 2,465 feet long, opened December 16, 1953, with governors John S. Fine and Alfred E. Driscoll presiding over the inaugural ceremony.
Originally carrying US 611, the bridge became part of Interstate 80 in 1959, linking the eastern and western United States across the Delaware River.
A pedestrian walkway on the New Jersey side connects the Appalachian Trail’s northern terminus in Pennsylvania to New Jersey’s southern end, offering scenic river views.
